speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've mentioned fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. These symptoms are concerning for a systemic process, possibly involving the lymphatic system. Have you noticed any changes in your skin or any lumps elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your symptoms are worsening. To help narrow this down, have you experienced any persistent fever, or have you noticed any recent infections or new medications? Also, do you have a history of autoimmune diseases or recent travel?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying. Given the "fixed" nature of the supraclavicular node and the B-symptoms (weight loss, night sweats), this is highly suspicious for malignancy. I need to assess for hepatosplenomegaly and check your blood count. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, LDH, and ESR. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal ultrasound. REQUEST IMAGES: CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal. Lactate Dehydrogenase: Elevated. CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Biopsy of Cervical Lymph Node: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Physical Examination: Nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node; Splenomegaly detected without rebound tenderness.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma (suspected Hodgkin's or Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma).
